attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, stated as fact.

semantics.note: Keeps the $75B figure, the year-to-date window, and both companies' margin-projection cuts at end of 2025. It drops the 'between Google, Amazon and investors' breakdown, but the contract keeps it.

contract.note: Reading 'raised' as completed funding and 'end of 2025' as Q4 is an ordinary reading. Whether conditional Google and Amazon commitments count changes the total a lot, so the interpretation matters.

evidence.note: Company disclosure of the $30B Series G in February. One part of the total, not a complete year-to-date record.
Company disclosure: $5B from Amazon now, up to $20B more later. Separates money received from future money but is not a complete ledger.
Secondary report: Google puts in at least $10B, up to $40B if performance targets are met. Shows terms, not the amount closed by May 26.
February report of lower OpenAI margin targets. Does not date the revision to Q4 2025 and does not cover Anthropic.

reviews.rationale: The packet confirms about $45B in money received ($30B + $5B + $10B) plus conditional commitments, but no complete closing record. So it cannot confirm or rule out $75B completed by May 26. No dated Q4 2025 margin-projection revisions were obtained for either company (key sources returned 403). Neither part of the claim is settled.

attribution.note: Zitron asks and answers the question himself, in his own voice.

semantics.note: 'Not really!' is a firm, slightly softened no, not a probability. 'LLMs cannot write all code' captures it.

contract.note: The plain reading, that current LLMs cannot reliably complete every programming task correctly, is an ordinary reading of 'write all code' in context. It is not stretched either way.

evidence.note: May 14, 2026 preprint with executable tests. The best agent (Claude Opus 4.7) resolved about 61%, so contemporary systems left many coding tasks unsolved.

reviews.rationale: A reproducible benchmark from inside the observation window shows leading coding agents failing a large share of executable maintenance tasks. That meets the support condition, and the packet has no evidence of reliable completion across all programming tasks.

attribution.note: Zitron's own prediction in his own post.

semantics.note: Firm 'will', so it is a forecast with no deadline. It is heavily rhetorical ('gladly', 'gruesome'), but the financial core can in principle be scored.

contract.note: The $200B floor and the write-down measure are evaluator choices, but reasonable ones. They do not change the result, because nothing can be scored yet.

evidence.note: September 2026 report of Burry warning about future write-offs. It is another person's forecast, not a record of actual losses.

reviews.rationale: The forecast has no deadline, and no conclusive event in the packet shows $200B or more in reconciled AI losses followed by a severe downturn. Absence of the event so far is not failure. The claim stays open.

semantics.note: 'Demand' refers to the compute and data center demand cited from NVIDIA and Samsung guidance. 'Almost entirely' is preserved.

contract.note: The sector-wide reading matches the context. Using Q1 2026 as the period is an evaluator choice, but a reasonable one. No numeric threshold was invented.

evidence.note: Columbia preprint describes a mix of debt, equity, and operating cash, but gives no measured debt share for Q1 purchases.
PIMCO says AI build-out is increasingly debt-financed while hyperscaler leverage stays low. It gives no funding-share measure for Q1.

reviews.rationale: Both sources suggest mixed financing, with a growing debt share, but neither measures what share of Q1 2026 AI compute purchases was funded by debt. Without that breakdown the claim is neither supported nor contradicted.
